paragraphs.text: Live preset inventory for DeepSeek Harness: which preset holds which tools, MCP servers and skills,
in the Web GUI and from the CLI.
# dsh-preset-inspector

A read-only panel in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI that answers **"what is actually
inside preset X?"

** — and a pair of CLIs that answer the same question from a
terminal, plus one that moves a plugin

of CLIs that answer the same question from a
terminal, plus one that moves a plugin between presets.
## Why

A DSH profile runs several **agent presets** (Standard, Web, Media, Creative, …).
Each preset declar

es a complete child plugin list, and those rows decide the tools,
skills and MCP servers a session g
ets. Three things make that hard to see:

- The GUI picker shows preset **names**, not contents.
- A request header lists tool **names**, not

which preset granted them.
- A plugin installed as a **bundle** mounts at host level, so its tools a

ppear in
*every* preset — silently, and at token cost in every session.
This plugin makes all of it visible, and gives you one command to change it.
## What it shows

- **Matrix** — every capability (tool, conditional tool, MCP server, skill) against
every preset.
-

**Per preset** — tools grouped by the plugin that registers them, conditional
tools with the reason

each is not guaranteed, MCP servers and their endpoints,
skill roots with counts and names, and ever

y composition row with its state.
- **Live** — the data comes from the running preset registry, so a

preset that
failed to mount shows up with its diagnostic instead of hiding.
## How it works

The host half reads `ctx.agentPresets` — the same registry the GUI picker uses —
flattens each prese

t's `config.plugins`, resolves every module to its package
directory and attributes the tool names t

hat package registers. Host rows that
register tools are added to every preset, because `ToolRuntime

.view(scope)`
inherits ancestor layers.

The browser half is a **client module** (`exports["./client"]`): the host ships the
snapshot as `glo

balThis.__dshPresets` through a `global` index-injection row, and
the client module renders it. No b
undler, no route, no auth work.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or from a checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then add `dsh-preset-inspector` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` and r

estart `dsh web`. A **▦ Presets** button
appears at the bottom-right of the GUI.
It registers no tools of its own, so it costs a session nothing in tool schemas.
## CLIs (optional, no install required)

`bin/` carries the terminal side of the same idea. `node bin/dsh-presets` and
`node bin/dsh-preset-p
lugin`, or symlink them onto your `PATH`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Both read `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config`, which composes the profile and
exits without binding

a port — so they work while a server is running, and they
never touch one.

`dsh-preset-plugin` writes with a backup, recomposes to verify, and rolls back if
the composition fa

ils. A `move` followed by `everywhere` leaves the file
byte-identical.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer in the 0.2.1 line (verified against
`0.2.1-rc.4` on 2026-10

-31; it reads the preset registry API).
- Node `>= 22`.
No runtime dependencies.
